objective: Diagnose long activity gaps and build an independent strategy challenge with evidence-based continue, pivot, reject and defer decisions.
hypothesis: Runtime continuity monitoring and pre-experiment strategy review address different failures; deterministic gates plus calibrated independent review can expose both without adding an always-on agent fleet.
baseline: Policyv2 has artifact and process review, but no explicit runtime goal before today, no strategy decision contract, and multiple unexplained multi-hour activity gaps.

result.summary: Added independent pre-experiment strategy contracts, evidence pins and phase-start rejection gates plus a metadata-only activity diagnostic.20affected tests pass; real-session diagnostic runs. Power events closely match the multi-hour gaps. Restored90%-used instruction and activated a runtime continuation goal. Existing evaluator gains strategy instructions; README diagram updated. Decision quality and stall recovery are not yet demonstrated.
result.nextAction: Make the two user-defined goals authoritative and enforce README architecture synchronization, then prospectively pilot the strategy gate on artwork.

findings: Sleep events closely match gaps, but activity metadata cannot diagnose all backend delay or recover a sleeping host. Initial coarse audit omitted custom tool events and was corrected.
Independent strategy challenge supports a minimal pilot; contract tests prove gate behavior, not critical-thinking quality.
Audit, workflow changes and user steering exceeded the initial phase estimate. Future contracts must keep goal visibility and documentation synchronization in the same change.

actions.summary: Keep evidence-pinned strategy gates and bounded health reporting with explicit limits.
Treat the two goals as equal, pin acceptance criteria, and make stale architecture diagrams fail checks.

review.nextImprovement: Use a real independently reviewed next-phase packet; preserve both goals in every startup brief and reject documentation drift.
